# `sesam reveal --force-diverged` takes the incoming version of every diverged
# secret, but unlike --all it keeps edits the merge did not touch.

sesam-repo admin base.txt theirs.txt edited.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt local
exec sesam add s local --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s local'

exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s'

exec git checkout master
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: add bob'

! exec git merge topic
cp $TMPDIR/edited.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/edited.txt local
exec sesam status
stdout '! s'
stdout 'M local'

exec sesam reveal --force-diverged
stderr 'discarded your unsealed edits in 1 secret'
stderr 'sesam:   s'
stderr 'kept 1 edited secret'
stderr 'sesam:   local'
exec cat s
stdout 'THEIRS'
exec cat local
stdout 'MY-EDIT'

exec git commit -m 'merge topic'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'THEIRS'

-- base.txt --
BASE
-- theirs.txt --
THEIRS
-- edited.txt --
MY-EDIT
